argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Dialectical reconstruction with thesis, antithesis, synthesis, and critical evaluation

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: Strong: engages objections and alternative interpretations
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High: all sections contribute to the central thesis

distinctions_drawn: False conceit of wisdom vs. genuine ignorance
explicit_definitions_given: Piety as service (hyperesia) aiming at the work (ergon) of soul-cultivation
Elenchus as epistemic purification of false conceit of wisdom
Daimonion as internalized divine voice of moral restraint

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Raises two major objections and responds to each: theological instability and elenctic nihilism
objections_raised: Socratic theology is unstable between polytheism and monotheism, making his defense disingenuous
Elenchus is purely destructive, leaving no positive knowledge and paralyzing moral agency

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Primary textual quotations, conceptual analysis, historical contextualization, and philosophical reconstruction

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Objective moral realism with rational theology
philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Intellectualist and internalist: virtue is knowledge; divine authority is rational and internalized
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Philosophy as sacred practice; care of the soul; epistemic purification

structural_organization.structure_type: Seven-part essay: Introduction, Parts I–V, Conclusion; each part has a distinct dialectical function

summary_of_core_decisions: The text reconstructs Socratic piety as a radical redefinition of divine service: from ritual transaction to philosophical soul-care. It uses the Euthyphro dilemma to establish the objective Good, the Apology to show philosophy as divine service, and the elenchus as sacred purification. It defends this reading against theological and methodological objections by appealing to the daimonion and internal moral authority, concluding that Socratic piety is the examined life.

thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Low: final paragraph is assertive and declarative
